objective: Retest whether the source-kind gain table's priority order matches delivered value, on a SECOND cohort of closed docket items whose outcomes are graded by an agent that has not read the first lookback, with the perturbation-robustness check the chief declined on the first cohort run there instead
rationale: This item exists because a check was refused for the right reason and the refusal has a dated successor rather than a quiet death. The gain-table note of 2026-08-10 measured mean delivered value per source kind across 114 closed items and found the table's order inverted at both ends, with challenge scored highest and delivering least and report scored lowest and delivering more. The chief ruled no re-pointing of the weights on that cohort, on the grounds that fitting seven weights to 114 outcomes graded by one agent is the in-sample move the lab refuses everywhere else, and separately declined the perturbation-robustness check on the per-kind means because sharpening a number already declined would invite action on it. Both rulings are correct and this proposal does not relitigate either. What it does is name the conditions under which the question becomes answerable. Three defects in the first cohort are fixable only by a second one. First, the outcomes were graded by a single agent from each item's own outcome field, with no independent check, so every per-kind mean inherits one reader's judgement. Second, the grading is hindsight by construction: the grader knew what each item delivered before assigning a value, which is unavoidable in a lookback and avoidable in a forward-scored cohort. Third, the cells are small where it matters most, and the note says so against its own headline: challenge carries n of 4, two of which are duplicate filings of the same rung, and dropping those two moves challenge from last to first on n of 2. A finding that reverses on two rows is not a finding about a weight. The second cohort fixes all three at once. The grader is an agent with no prior contact with the first lookback and no access to it during grading, the rubric is the published 0 to 3 scale so the two cohorts are commensurable, and outcome values are assigned before any per-kind aggregation is computed. Only then does the perturbation check run, on both cohorts, and only then is a weight amendment even discussable. The already-filed confidence-line change is the other half of the timing: once pre-registrations carry a numeric confidence, the ordinal proxy behind the companion numerator result is replaced by a stated probability and the same cohort serves both questions. Axis A: report-kind at zero solver cost. Axis B: 0. Axis C: 0, and it changes no scored column and no weight.
citations: The gain-table inversion note of 2026-08-10 and the chief ruling on it

cost_basis: measured; the first cohort's identical work took zero solver time and the second is the same shape at the same size, a grading pass over outcome fields already on disk followed by arithmetic, so no solver time is spent and no case is opened
expected_knowledge_gain: Three outcomes and the ruling differs in each. One: the second cohort reproduces the first cohort's per-kind ordering, in which case the inversion is a property of the table rather than of one grader, the perturbation check has something worth sharpening, and a weight amendment becomes discussable on out-of-sample evidence. Two: it does not reproduce, which would say the per-kind means are a grader artefact and would retire the whole line, protecting the charter from an amendment it never needed. Three: the two graders disagree on the item-level values badly enough that neither ordering can be trusted, which is the most useful outcome of the three, because it would put a number on how reproducible this lab's own outcome grading is and that number governs every lookback the lab will ever run, including the one already filed against the ranking numerator.
in_sample_verdict: This item exists to remove an in-sample defect rather than to add one. Nothing is fitted and no weight is changed by it; the grading rubric is fixed and published before the second cohort is graded, the grader is blind to the first cohort's results, and the per-kind aggregation is computed only after every item-level value is committed. If the ordering is used to justify a weight change later, that change is a separate filing and owes its own criterion.
sequencing: WAITS. Not dispatchable now and deliberately so: the second cohort does not exist yet, because it needs a further tranche of docket items closed after 2026-08-10 so that its outcomes were never available to the first lookback's author. It is filed now, priced at zero, so the declined check has a dated home rather than being rediscovered. It becomes dispatchable when the docket has closed enough further items to grade, and it should be sequenced alongside the confidence-line change so one grading pass serves both.
gate: A second cohort of closed docket items, all closed after 2026-08-10, graded on the published 0 to 3 rubric by an agent with no prior contact with the first lookback and no access to it while grading. Per-kind mean delivered value is computed for both cohorts, the item-level agreement between the two graders is reported on the overlap if any exists, and the perturbation-robustness check is run on the per-kind means of both. The result is reported whatever it says, including the case where the two cohorts disagree. No weight is amended by this item under any outcome.
